speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a psychiatric condition and have developed a new movement disorder; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed if these movements started while you were taking any psychiatric medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very helpful; since you were prescribed risperidone two months ago and noticed the movements shortly after, have you experienced stiffness, tremors, or any involuntary writhing movements like chorea? Also, have you noticed any changes in your voice volume or facial expressions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Dystonia is less likely given the description of restlessness and fidgeting; the clinical picture is most consistent with Akathisia secondary to risperidone. Given your history of fidgeting and an inability to sit still, this is a classic presentation of medication-induced akathisia. Do you feel an inner sense of agitation or an urgent need to move that is difficult to control?
